title: The Fire Element: Meaning, Years and Personality in the Chinese Zodiac
seo_title: Fire Element in the Chinese Zodiac: Meaning, Years, Personality
description: What the Fire element means in the Chinese five elements: its season, direction and colour, every Fire year from 1944 to 2035, how Fire relates to the other elements, and the Fire personality.
lead: Fire is one of the five elements of Chinese tradition, alongside Wood, Earth, Metal and Water. Here is what Fire stands for, which birth years belong to it, and how it works with the other four elements.
card_text: What the Fire element means, every Fire year from 1944 to 2035, and the Fire personality.

paras: Think of a lantern in the dark or the midday sun in summer: light, warmth and movement that everyone around can feel. Fire is the element of energy at its peak. It brightens, it spreads, it brings people together around it, and it needs fuel and care to keep burning steadily rather than flaring up and fading.

In Chinese the five elements are called wuxing, and Fire is huo. As Wikipedia's article on wuxing notes, the word was first translated into English as the Five Elements, but the idea is less about physical substances than about processes and change. That is why some scholars prefer translations such as five phases or five agents. Fire is best understood as a stage in a cycle, a kind of energy, rather than only a material.
Traditional Chinese cosmology links each element with a season, a direction, a colour and more. The New World Encyclopedia lists these correspondences for Fire:

Every Chinese year is named by pairing one of ten Heavenly Stems with one of twelve Earthly Branches, the system the Hong Kong Observatory describes in its guide to the stems and branches. The branch gives the year's animal; the stem gives its element. Two stems belong to Fire: Bing, the yang form, and Ding, the yin form, as the table of stems in Wikipedia's article on the sexagenary cycle shows.

Because the ten stems repeat every ten years, each element covers two years in a row, once a decade. Wikipedia notes that 1984 was a Jia-zi year, the start of the present sixty-year cycle; counting from there gives a simple rule: Fire years end in 6 or 7. These are the Fire years from 1944 to 2035:
after: We are living in Fire years right now: 2026 is the Fire Horse year, and the Fire Goat year begins at Chinese New Year on 6 February 2027. The Farmers’ Almanac describes both as Fire years. After them, the next Fire years are 2036 and 2037.

One important detail: the Chinese year starts at Chinese New Year, in late January or February, not on 1 January. Someone born in January 2016, before that year's Chinese New Year, still belongs to the previous year and its element. Our zodiac sign checker uses the exact new-year date for every year.

paras: Each element appears twice in the cycle, once in a yang form and once in a yin form. Bing years are yang Fire, and they always fall on yang animals (Rat, Tiger, Dragon, Horse, Monkey and Dog). Ding years are yin Fire, and they always fall on yin animals (Ox, Rabbit, Snake, Goat, Rooster and Pig). In the list above, the years ending in 6 are yang and the years ending in 7 are yin.
Yang is traditionally the more outward, active side and yin the more inward, receptive side. Neither is better than the other: both are needed, and every element moves between them.

sections.h2: How Fire works with the other elements
paras: The five elements are linked by two traditional cycles, which the New World Encyclopedia and Wikipedia both describe. In the generating cycle, each element feeds the next: Wood feeds Fire, Fire creates Earth, Earth bears Metal, Metal carries Water and Water nourishes Wood. In the overcoming cycle, each element keeps another in check: Wood parts Earth, Earth absorbs Water, Water quenches Fire, Fire melts Metal and Metal chops Wood. For Fire, that means:
list: Wood supports Fire: Wood feeds Fire, as dry branches keep a flame alive.
Fire supports Earth: Fire creates Earth, leaving ash that becomes soil.
Fire restrains Metal: Fire melts Metal, as a forge softens iron so it can be shaped.
after: In compatibility readings, elements that follow each other in the generating cycle are traditionally said to support each other, and those linked by the overcoming cycle are said to need more balance. Our five elements guide shows both cycles for all five elements, and the compatibility calculator compares the signs of any two birth dates.

paras: In our readings on this site, the Fire element describes a style of energy that colours a person's zodiac sign. We describe it like this: Fire brings heat, motion, and visibility. People born in a Fire year rarely blend into the background: they tend to speak with conviction, move quickly, and inspire people around them to act. This makes them natural leaders in a crisis or a bold new venture. The challenge is sustaining that intensity: Fire personalities can burn through relationships or opportunities fast if they don't pair their passion with patience.

Remember that the element is only one part of a traditional reading, alongside the animal, yin or yang, and in fuller readings the month, day and hour of birth. Two people with the same element can be very different, and the zodiac is a cultural tradition for reflection and fun, not a scientific test of character.
Whatever your own element, traditional advice uses Fire as a reminder of certain qualities:
list: Share your energy: Fire is the element of warmth and visibility, so traditional advice links it with gatherings, celebrations and speaking up.
Pace yourself: a steady flame lasts longer than a bonfire.
Pair passion with patience, especially before big decisions.

faq: Which years are Fire years in the Chinese zodiac?
Years ending in 6 or 7, for example 2006, 2007, 2026 and 2027. The year starts at Chinese New Year, so January and early February births may belong to the previous year.
What season, direction and colour go with Fire?
Traditionally Fire goes with summer, south and red.
Wood, in the generating cycle: Wood feeds Fire, as dry branches keep a flame alive. Fire in turn supports Earth.
Is my element the same as my zodiac animal?

No. Your animal comes from the year's Earthly Branch and your element from its Heavenly Stem. Each animal can have any of the five elements, so the same animal and element combination returns only every sixty years.
